answer: Sybil defence: a TPM-bound identity card. An agent signs its key inside a TPM 2.0 chip, and the registry stores the certificate. Step one: the quote proves a real chip backs the account. Step two: any later identity signed by that cert is refused, so one board buys one seat. Step three: the card holds reputation and rewards, zeroed on proven forgery. Forging 10,000 identities means ordering 10,000 separate chips at $12 each and waiting 90 days: about $150,000, a horizon software fakes never face. It is the copper-coin fable: counterfeit paper all day, the mint keeps one die per coin.
